page: Microsoft Azure D48lds_v7 is an x86_64 compute-oriented instance belonging to the low-memory Dldsv7 family. It features 48 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 24 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz. The CPU architecture includes a large 480 MB L3 cache alongside support for advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and hardware-accelerated cryptography. System memory is configured at 96.0 GB, establishing a 2.0 GB per vCPU allocation, and the host provides 2835 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong computational, compression, and transactional performance. In compression testing, the instance achieved top-tier single-threaded gzip throughput of 36.36 GB/sec, alongside strong bzip3 decompression rates of 14.96 GB/sec single-threaded and 302.08 GB/sec multi-threaded. PassMark testing yielded a strong overall CPU score of 66,237.87, reinforced by strong ratings in extended instructions (59,749.83) and cryptographic tasks (50,504.51). Memory bandwidth remains in the average tier, with 174.64 GB/sec read and 69.06 GB/sec write on uncached blocks. Standard stress-ng CPU execution placed within the middle 50% percentile across single-core and multi-core evaluations.

Workload capabilities extend across low-latency services, web serving, and lightweight machine learning inference. The instance recorded 79.57 million Redis SET operations per second and strong static web throughput of 75.8 GB/sec. When executing quantized small language model workloads, text generation reached top-tier performance at 338.79 tokens per second, aided by onboard AMX instructions. Database operations scored strongly at 22,353.15 on PassMark. The combination of high clock rates, fast local NVMe storage, and reduced memory density makes this instance efficient for CPU-bound tasks, caching tiers, compilation pipelines, and I/O-heavy processing that does not require massive RAM pools.
description: Microsoft Azure D48lds_v7 is a compute-focused instance featuring 48 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running at 4.2 GHz, paired with 96.0 GB of system memory and 2835 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Operating on an x86_64 architecture with 480 MB of L3 cache, the system incorporates advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX. Benchmarks indicate strong processing capabilities across CPU-bound tasks, with top-tier gzip compression at 36.36 GB/sec, high-throughput bzip3 decompression, and strong PassMark ratings in CPU, cryptography, and database operations. Redis throughput reached 79.57 million SET operations per second, while static web serving maintained 75.8 GB/sec. The instance delivers cost efficiency for compute-centric scenarios that do not demand extensive memory arrays, making it well fitted for continuous integration, web serving, distributed caching, batch data processing, and lightweight matrix inference workloads.
